item.title: Shapiro spikes in driven quantum fluids
item.description: arXiv:2611.05477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Periodic driving of a Josephson junction produces resonant transport signatures known as Shapiro spikes, conventionally described by effective circuit models. Here, we demonstrate Shapiro spikes in a neutral quantum fluid using simulations of a potential-biased atomic Josephson junction. The dc-current resonances follow the expected Bessel-function scaling, including the suppression and revival of individual resonances with increasing modulation strength. We uncover their microscopic mechanism by showing that the phase-winding frequency develops finite plateaus at integer multiples of the drive frequency. These phase-locked states are sustained by quantized-vortex nucleation and the associated $2\pi$ phase slips. Remarkably, within a locking plateau, the dc current and density transfer can reverse direction while the phase-winding frequency remains locked to the drive, giving rise to negative-mobility transport. Our results establish a microscopic link between vortex-mediated phase slips, Shapiro resonances, and anomalous transport in a neutral quantum fluid, revealing how quantized vortices convert resonant transport into phase-locked dynamics with negative mobility.
item.dc:creator: Vijay Pal Singh, Ludwig Mathey, Luigi Amico

item.title: Coherence Spreading Law in Quenched Homogeneous Bose Gases
item.description: arXiv:2611.05775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate nonequilibrium coherence spreading in quenched homogeneous bosonic gases both analytically and numerically. Our ensemble-averaged Gross-Pitaevskii trajectory approach and kinetic analysis confirm the linear-in-time growth of the squared coherence length, and explicitly give the spreading-law dependence on the ratio of initial energy to healing energy. When the ratio is relatively small, the squared coherence length grows at a universal rate determined by the ratio of Planck's constant to the particle mass, insensitive to interaction strength and initial momentum distributions. However, our further calculations uncover fundamental limitations to such universality and establish its phase boundaries governed by low system energies, weak interparticle interactions and many-body integrability. Our theory fully reproduces the key experimental signatures and resolves the puzzle of the dynamical origin of the recently observed universal coherence-spreading speed limit [Nature 647, 608-612 (2025)]. Going beyond existing experimental observations, we provide some testable predictions for ultracold-atom experiments and clarify the conditions for the emergence of universal coherent dynamics in nonequilibrium bosonic many-body systems.
item.dc:creator: Yi Cao, Li-Chen Zhao, Jie Liu

item.title: Analytic two-body density-matrix spectrum of the Fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas
item.description: arXiv:2611.05820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The two-body density matrix (TBDM) of a quantum many-body system provides information about particle correlations, e.g., pairing. In this work, we derive the complete spectrum of the TBDM of the fermionic Tonks-Girardeau gas using its exact ground-state wavefunction in second quantization. We obtain analytical expressions for all eigenvalues and eigenvectors for an arbitrary number of particles and identify two different types of eigenstates: collective states, formed by superpositions of paired momentum modes, and single-determinant states. We provide a physical interpretation of this structure, explaining the origin of the different eigenstates and their degeneracies. We further derive an asymptotic expansion for the largest eigenvalue, improving on previous estimates and analytically confirming its linear scaling with the particle number, thereby indicating off-diagonal long-range order. For the high-index collective states, we obtain simpler expressions for the eigenvalues and eigenvectors, showing that the eigenvalues decay as $n^{-4}$ and that the eigenvectors become independent of the number of particles. Finally, we discuss the connection between the collective states and an effective description in terms of composite bosons, whose spectral properties suggest a behavior consistent with Tan's contact for interacting bosonic systems.
item.dc:creator: Abel Rojo-Franc\`{a}s, Joan Martorell, Francesc Sabater, Bruno Juli\'{a}-D\'{i}az

item.title: Majorana-like Josephson branch structure in one-dimensional transport of cold atoms
item.description: arXiv:2611.06693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study phase-controlled transport through a one-dimensional channel of attractively interacting fermions connecting two three-dimensional BCS reservoirs. The competition between channel phase stiffness and pair tunnelling at the two contacts results in the emergence of two $4\pi$-periodic families of stationary states, characterised by symmetric or asymmetric phase drops at the boundaries. Advancing the reservoir phase difference by $2\pi$ exchanges these families so that the equilibrium energy remains $2\pi$ periodic, while the $4\pi $ periodicity might be attained in a diabatic regime. This structure admits a formal description in terms of two boundary Majorana operators, combining into a nonlocal fermion mode. Renormalization-group analysis shows that quantum fluctuations and phase slips are suppressed in the zero-temperature thermodynamic limit, preserving the branch crossings. The predicted branch exchange, metastable currents, and sweep-rate-dependent switching provide experimentally testable signatures of Majorana-like Josephson branch physics in a gapless interacting channel.
item.dc:creator: Rory Whelan, Dimitri M. Gangardt, Igor V. Lerner

item.title: Fluctuating Hydrodynamics of Quantum Fluids from the Nonlinear Fokker-Planck Equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06485v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Starting from the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation (NFPE), we establish the fluctuating hydrodynamics for quantum fluids. We also investigate the corresponding stochastic thermodynamics and derive the associated fluctuation theorems. We then apply this framework to both fermionic and bosonic systems. For the ideal Fermi gas, we study the electrical conduction and reveal a resistance proportional to the product of temperature and the density of states at the Fermi surface. For bosonic fluids, we analyze the relaxation time characterizing the critical slowing down phenomenon and identify three distinct scaling behaviors corresponding to the non-interacting, repulsive interaction, and attractive interaction regimes. Overall, this work provides a experimentally verifiable phenomenological description for the dynamics of quantum fluids and demonstrates the applicability of the nonlinear Fokker-Planck equation in characterizing such systems.
item.dc:creator: Mingjian Gu, Zhaoyu Fei, Xiaoguang Wang

item.title: Stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.06528v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In quantum many-body physics and quantum field theory, it is often assumed that gapped systems remain gapped under sufficiently weak local perturbations. However, to what extent this assumption holds is elusive, except for some special systems. In this work, we examine the stability of energy gap of macroscopic quantum matter that is only subject to two physically natural conditions, locality and translation invariance. We first show that in any spatial dimension, there are gapped local Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap, i.e., they become gapless under certain arbitrarily weak local perturbation in the thermodynamic limit. We then prove that for both spin and fermionic systems in one dimension, such Hamiltonians with an unstable gap must not only break translation invariance but also be fine-tuned. We further show that in any dimension greater than one, there are fine-tuned local translation invariant Hamiltonians with a unique ground state and an unstable gap. These results greatly sharpen our understanding of the fundamental problem of the stability of quantum phases of matter. We also discuss implications of our results on, for example, anyon superconductivity and higher-form symmetries.
item.dc:creator: Kangle Li, Liujun Zou

item.title: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays
item.description: arXiv:2611.06613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Blackbody radiation (BBR) poses a central challenge for quantum science with Rydberg atoms. By driving transitions to nearby opposite-parity states, BBR shortens Rydberg lifetimes and has long been suspected to trigger "avalanche" events known to cause correlated atom loss. Here, we suppress avalanche decay and establish BBR as its dominant trigger using a Rydberg atom array that operates either cryogenically or at room temperature. A $45~\text{K}$ radiation shield reduces ambient BBR, extending Rydberg $nS$ lifetimes for $n$ ranging from 50 to 75. BBR-induced decay rates are suppressed by 30%-50%, corresponding to an effective blackbody temperature $T_{\rm eff}\approx190~\text{K}$. This enables controlled comparisons of Rydberg-dressed atom arrays operating in different BBR environments. Arrays of up to 70 atoms demonstrate cryogenically suppressed avalanche rates, tracking the suppression in BBR-induced decay, for both $n=50$ and $n=60$ dressing. A parameter-free rate model agrees with the measured avalanche rates after accounting for frequency-dependent cryogenic shielding, photoionization-triggered avalanches, laser phase noise, BBR decay channels, and Rydberg interaction effects. We demonstrate a quantitative description of avalanche decay and show that improved BBR shielding should further suppress correlated loss to the $T_\text{eff}=45~\text{K}$ achievable in the current apparatus. Our results establish a route to mitigating correlated errors that otherwise impede fault-tolerant operation in neutral-atom quantum processors.
item.dc:creator: Zhenpu Zhang, Brendan P. Marsh, Ting You Tan, Quinn Manning, Daniel H. Slichter, Adam M. Kaufman, Cindy A. Regal

item.title: Stability and mixed phases of three-component droplets in one dimension
item.description: arXiv:2601.04950v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explore the ground state properties and excitation spectra of one-dimensional, three-component bosonic mixtures, where two majority components form a self-bound droplet coupled to a third, minority component. Within a self-consistent Lee-Huang-Yang framework, we identify distinct mixed self-bound droplet phases and characterize their phase transitions through variations of either the particle number of the majority components or the intercomponent coupling. The ensuing phases demonstrate that the minority component is untrapped, partially trapped, or fully trapped by the majority droplet species. These states are characterized by their binding energies captured by the chemical potentials and their low-amplitude excitation spectrum, including mode crossings at the particle-emission threshold. We further derive effective reduced models in the high-imbalance limit, which accurately reproduce the numerically computed ground states, while providing analytical insights into the role of quantum fluctuations. Our results establish the stability and structure of mixed droplet phases provide experimentally relevant signatures for their identification.
item.dc:creator: I. A. Englezos, E. G. Charalampidis, P. Schmelcher, S. I. Mistakidis

item.title: Density Modulations of Zero Sound
item.description: arXiv:2602.04612v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the density modulation of an interacting Fermi gas caused by the uniform motion of an impurity at zero temperature. For strong enough interaction among Fermi atoms, the modulation propagates thanks to the excitation of the collective zero sound mode if the impurity speed is above the zero sound threshold. We are able to assess, via a semi-analytic evaluation, the extent of the zero sound contribution to the density oscillation over and above the incoherent background of particle-hole excitations. Given the strong dependence of the results on the features of the gas interaction potential, we also analyze how they vary depending on its strength, range and shape.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo Pisani

item.title: Emergent thermal fluctuations and non-Hermitian phase transitions in open photon condensates
item.description: arXiv:2603.21927v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein condensates of photons in optical resonators have been shown theoretically to exist as a long-lived, yet metastable state stabilized by a ghost attractor, despite continuous driving [Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 053402 (2025)]. Here we analyze the properties of this metastable condensate as well as the relaxation dynamics into and out of this state by means of the Lindblad master-equation approach, treating the condensate and the equal-time, noncondensed fluctuations on the same footing. Despite its nonequilibrium origin, the quasistationary condensate exhibits thermal behavior in that the order-parameter fluctuations scale with system size as in thermodynamic equilibrium, and the photon-number distribution in multimode resonators is in excellent agreement with a Bose-Einstein distribution. A linear stability analysis further reveals the presence of several exceptional points, resulting in multiple non-Hermitian phase transitions associated with the relaxation dynamics into and out of the metastable condensate. These behaviors reconcile apparently contradictory experimental results.
item.dc:creator: Moritz Janning, Roman Kramer, Aya Abouelela, Michael Turaev, Sayak Ray, Johann Kroha

item.title: Shapiro steps of superfluid Fermi gases in a ring trap across the BCS--BEC crossover
item.description: arXiv:2605.17940v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the transport properties of a superfluid Fermi gas confined in a ring trap with a moving potential barrier across the Bardeen-Cooper-Schrieffer (BCS) to Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) crossover. Employing time-dependent Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) equations, we simulate the dynamics of a Josephson junction biased by both DC and AC currents. Over a wide range of interaction strengths, the barrier-velocity dependence of the chemical potential difference exhibits low-order plateau structures, consistent with Shapiro steps, with fitted levels close to integer multiples of $\hbar\omega/2$ within the phase-coherent regime. This factor of $1/2$ reflects our convention of defining the chemical potential per single fermion in the BdG framework. Microscopic analysis reveals that these fundamental steps originate from synchronized phase slips mediated by periodic soliton generation at the barrier. Our findings clarify the role of interaction regimes in the nonequilibrium phase dynamics of ring-trapped fermionic superfluids and provide microscopic insights relevant to future studies of atomtronic systems with nontrivial topology.
item.dc:creator: Hikaru Kuriki, Masaya Kunimi, Tetsuro Nikuni

item.title: Vortices in a two-dimensional fermionic superfluid
item.description: arXiv:2611.05017v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantized vortices are a hallmark of superfluidity. They have proven to be an indispensable probe for systems ranging from superfluid helium to type-II superconductors. In ultracold two-dimensional (2D) Fermi gases, where phase fluctuations are enhanced and the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) mechanism governs the superfluid transition, their observation has remained elusive. Here, we report on the controlled creation of quantized vortices in a homogeneous 2D gas in the BEC--BCS crossover. By continuously tuning the velocity of two moving obstacles, we observe quantized steps in the absolute vortex charge. Matter-wave interferometry reveals the characteristic phase winding, quantized in units of $2\pi$. Measurements on 2D and 3D gases show a striking difference: only in 2D does the vortex number grow with temperature, reflecting thermal activation of BKT vortex pairs. Our approach provides evidence of fermionic superfluidity in 2D and offers a means to study BKT physics, vortex-controlled transport and resistance, as well as to detect unconventional superfluidity in spin-imbalanced 2D gases.
item.dc:creator: Artak Mkrtchyan, Hans Leonard Michel, Moritz von Usslar, Ren\'e Henke, Cesar R. Cabrera, Henning Moritz

item.title: Phonons under confinement: Finite Hilbert space, coarse-grained $U(1)$ charge and a new transport mechanism
item.description: arXiv:2607.14232v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An important feature of solid-state or cold atom systems in low dimensions is the restricted oscillations of ionic/atomic degrees of freedom in the confining directions, for which the conventional phonon from canonical quantization is not an ideal description. In this work we propose a general recipe to introduce this feature to otherwise unrestricted systems by mapping displacement fields to spin degrees of freedom, dubbed "soft-corization". In the strong-confinement limit $S=1/2$, we demonstrate the validity of the approach with a harmonic chain; the results lead to a gapped fermionic model showing the absence of acoustic modes as a signature of the confinement of the entire chain. Despite the non-conserved total particle number in the presence of nearest-neighbor parings, the model holds a coarse-grained $U(1)$ symmetry with conserved "polarization charge" in the absence of nearest-neighbor hopping. This enables a new transport mechanism via "dimer-tumbling" instead of single-particle hopping. We then introduce a short-range interaction via anharmonicity; for energy scales slightly above the gap, it leads to a (quantum) phase transition to a nonreciprocal state carrying dimer current and heat current with spontaneous time reversal symmetry breaking of the type $\hat{T}^2=+1$. The non-reciprocity can be probed by measuring the change of inductance due to gauge fields in and out of the ordered phase.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Gao, K. A. Muttalib
